title: Legacy CPAT bugs and the CPAT-AI register v1.1.0 (workbook v1.1.0)

definitions.definition: Legacy bug: legacy CPAT does not compute what it means to (a wrong row, a double application, a dead reference, a blank read as 0 where a value is meant); the fix is a change of formulas, with a cell plan.
Prototype bug: a defect of the prototype itself, found during development or by Coded CPAT's replication (user 2026-10-29).
definitions.prototype: Fixed; an open one is listed with its fix, and Coded CPAT replicates it until the prototype is fixed.

definitions.definition: Documentation bug: the CPAT methodology documentation is wrong, missing or contradicts itself (an equation, a sign, a symbol, a unit, a reference); the models are not affected (user 2026-10-29).
definitions.prototype: Follows the workbooks; the documentation is to be corrected.

definitions.definition: Issue: legacy does what it means to, but the choice is open to question (a method, a default, a convention, the input data: area Data), or a limitation of the prototype. Priority: Major or Minor; data problems Very high (a bug fix covers them) or Extremely high (no cell plan possible; the prototype does exactly what legacy does).
definitions.prototype: Replicates it and tracks it; a departure only by user decision, recorded with the issue.

definitions.definition: Departure: a row of the prototype's LegacyDiff sheet that is not "Same" (a decision, a simplification, a part not built yet).
Upgrade: a possible improvement beyond legacy.

other_mitigation_areas.about: Population, GDP growth and the GDP-effect multipliers: everything downstream depends on them.
Price parameters, pass-through, VAT, consumer and producer subsidies, and the average-price reports.
Methane, flaring, waste and the local-pollutant emission factors and totals.
Regulation shares and adjustments, feebate inclusion and rates.
New and existing ETS, existing carbon taxes, coverage and the shadow prices.
Sector fuel-use blocks (aviation, other energy use, residential, road), exemptions and leakage, manual power investment.
Energy trade balance and current account.
Revenue rows and the revenue reports.
Manual-input blocks and the names that read them.

records.title: GDP effect added to GDP growth every year
records.description: The fiscal multipliers give the change of the GDP level; legacy adds that change to the growth rate every year, so a steady effect of 0.5% raises growth by 0.5 points a year and compounds (about +10% of GDP after 20 years instead of +0.5%). records.effect: A steady effect of 0.5% compounds to about +10% of GDP after 20 years, in every run with endogenous GDP effects (the NoPropData file strips these rows).
records.prototype: Fixed in v0.3.1: the GDP level is raised by the effect (growth from the ratio of level factors).
